title: Ga3+ Replacing of Fe3+ as a "Trojan Horse" Antimicrobial Strategy: Modeling the Process within Bacterial Catalase-Peroxidase KatG.
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
abstract: Replacement of Fe3+ by Ga3+ has emerged as a promising "Trojan horse" antimicrobial strategy in response to the growing threat of antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Because many bacterial proteins hijack host iron to sustain essential redox processes, substitution with redox inactive Ga3+, which closely resembles Fe3+ in ionic radius but possesses only one oxidation state, can disrupt their activity. Among potential targets, bacterial catalase-peroxidase shows particular sensitivity to Fe3+/Ga3+ exchange. However, the structural determinants and thermodynamic driving forces governing this substitution remain poorly understood. Here we combine ad hoc force field development, molecular dynamics simulations, alchemical free energy calculations, and QM/MM methods to elucidate the molecular basis of Fe3+/Ga3+ exchange in the bacterial catalase-peroxidase KatG. Our simulations show that the axial coordination environment of the heme B cofactor is largely preserved upon metal substitution, while the distal ligand dynamically alternates between histidine and a coordinated water molecule. Energy decomposition analysis reveals residue specific differences in electrostatic and van der Waals interactions following metal exchange. Free energy calculations indicate that substitution of iron by gallium in the KatG active site is thermodynamically favorable. The presence of a coordinated water molecule emerges as a key structural feature in both metalated states, while distinct binding patterns contribute differently to the overall thermodynamic driving force. These results provide an atomistic description of gallium mediated metal substitution in KatG and offer mechanistic insight into gallium-based antimicrobial strategies, supporting the rational design of new iron-mimetic antibacterial agents.

title: [Clinical outcomes of horse antithymocyte globulin-based immunosuppressive therapy for aplastic anemia at a single institution].
journal: [Rinsho ketsueki] The Japanese journal of clinical hematology
abstract: Horse antithymocyte globulin (hATG) has been available for the treatment of aplastic anemia (AA) in Japan since 2023. To evaluate the efficacy and safety of combination therapy with hATG, cyclosporine, and a thrombopoietin receptor agonist (TPO-RA), and determine the optimal steroid regimen for serum sickness prophylaxis. We retrospectively reviewed seven patients with AA who received hATG combined with cyclosporine and a thrombopoietin receptor agonist (TPO-RA; eltrombopag or romiplostim). The median age was 62 years. All patients achieved transfusion independence within 3 months (median day 35 for red blood cells and day 36 for platelets). Six patients remain alive and transfusion-independent, while one died of heart failure. The early dose-reduction regimen frequently failed because of serum sickness, necessitating a switch to the conventional method. hATG-based triple therapy led to rapid transfusion independence. Switching TPO-RAs may be effective in patients with a suboptimal response. The conventional method of steroid prophylaxis may be preferable.

title: Pregnancy outcome and associated factors following colic surgery in Thoroughbred broodmares.
journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
abstract: Colic surgery in pregnant broodmares raises concerns not only for maternal survival but also for fetal outcome. Although several studies have reported foaling rates after colic surgery and the influence of perioperative factors on pregnancy outcome, the findings remain inconsistent. This study aimed to determine the foaling rate following colic surgery in Thoroughbred broodmares and to evaluate the effects of perioperative factors and gestational stage on pregnancy outcome. Medical records of Thoroughbred broodmares that underwent colic surgery at Shadai Horse Clinic from 2014 to 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. Data collected included mare age, gestational stage, diagnosis category, intraoperative hypotension, hypoxemia, anesthetic maintenance technique (inhalation anesthesia alone or inhalation anesthesia combined with partial intravenous anesthesia), duration of general anesthesia, postoperative administration of altrenogest, postoperative complications (diarrhea and catheter-associated jugular phlebitis), postoperative signs of endotoxemia, and pregnancy outcome. The overall foaling rate was 69.6% (110/158). The occurrence of intraoperative hypotension in late-gestational mares (P=0.036) were significantly associated with negative pregnancy outcome in univariate analysis, whereas most other perioperative factors showed no significant association. The occurrence of intraoperative hypoxemia was significantly higher in the late-gestational mares, however it did not affect pregnancy outcome. In conclusion, the foaling rate following colic surgery in pregnant Thoroughbred broodmares was comparable to that reported in previous studies. These findings suggest that intraoperative hypotension may warrant particular attention in late-gestation mare undergoing colic surgery.

title: Evaluation of linkage disequilibrium, haplotype block structure, and historical effective population size in the Iranian Turkmen horse.
journal: Mammalian genome : official journal of the International Mammalian Genome Society
abstract: This study used the Illumina Equine SNP70 BeadChip to investigate whole-genome linkage disequilibrium (LD), haplotype block structure, and historical effective population size (Ne) of the Iranian Turkmen horse. Genotyping was performed on 70 samples, of which 62 passed quality control and were retained for analysis. We estimated the extent of LD using r2 and D' measures and characterized haplotype block structure and historical Ne. Gene Ontology (GO) and pathway enrichment analyses were performed to identify biological functions associated with genes within the detected haplotype blocks. Across all SNP pairs analyzed (distance ≤ 5 Mb), mean r2 was 0.04, while mean D' was 0.47. Mean r2 for the closest SNP pairs (<5 kb) was 0.49, indicating high LD at short distances. Because D' is sensitive to allele frequency and sample size, the interpretation focused primarily on r2. A total of 5,155 haplotype blocks were detected, mainly on chromosome 1, involving 16,553 SNPs and encompassing 29% of all SNPs in the genome. The estimated Ne decreased with increasing number of generations, indicating the need for adequate conservation measures to ensure the genetic diversity of this valuable breed. GO and pathway enrichment analysis of genes within the longest haplotype blocks showed significant overrepresentation of biological processes related to steroid metabolism, oxidative demethylation, apoptotic signaling, chemical carcinogenesis, and retinol metabolism. These findings suggest candidate biological processes that require further validation.

title: Ecdysterone concentrations in horses following treatment and withdrawal of this naturally occurring prohibited anabolic steroid.
journal: Veterinary journal (London, England : 1997)
abstract: The medicinal properties of ecdysterone, a steroid made by plants, insects, and internal parasites, have been exploited in traditional medicine for decades. As ecdysterone can increase muscle strength, it could benefit senior horses with muscle wasting. However, the wide availability of ecdysterone supplements is a concern for horseracing authorities, while the risk of environmental exposure to this prohibited substance presents a challenge for owners and trainers. This study examined ecdysterone concentrations in eight Standardbred horses following ecdysterone treatment, re-examined samples from another study using 17 horses, and compared ELISA values with mass spectrometry data to explore some unexpected results. Serum ecdysterone concentrations peaked at 36 ng/mL (median), 40 min after a single oral dose (5 mg/kgBW). A second peak occurred, likely due to enterohepatic recycling, between 2 and 24 h, varying markedly between horses and reaching 9-134 ng/mL. Concentrations returned to pre-treatment values in all horses after 32 h and no accumulation occurred in serum or faeces during 7 daily doses. Serum ecdysterone was persistently high (ca. 20 ng/mL) in one individual when measured by ELISA, but not by mass spectrometry, indicating likely interference with the antibody-based assay. Otherwise, the two analytical methods showed good agreement. Ecdysterone concentrations measured in 17 different horses four times in one day showed marked and sporadic spikes which appeared and disappeared within 40 min, suggesting an endogenous origin (e.g. from internal parasites). Additional studies are needed to understand this phenomenon, assist anti-doping authorities in setting a residue limit, and explore therapeutic opportunities in equine medicine.

title: Psychotropic Drug GST Interactions: In Vitro Inhibition, Molecular Docking, and Translational Potential in Cancer Therapy.
journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
abstract: Psychotropic drugs are widely used to treat mental disorders, but they also influence cellular pathways linked to cancer. One key enzyme, Glutathione S-transferase (GST), is involved in detoxification and drug resistance in tumors, making it a potential target in cancer therapy. This study examined the effects of selected psychotropic agents aripiprazole, fluoxetine hydrochloride, risperidone, haloperidol, and sodium valproate on GST activity derived from equine liver. Enzyme kinetics were assessed in vitro using 1-chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene (CDNB) as the substrate and ethacrynic acid (Kᵢ = 4.7 ± 0.8 nM) as the standard reference inhibitor. IC50 values were determined, and inhibition constants (Kᵢ) were calculated via Lineweaver-Burk plot analysis. The ranked Kᵢ values were as follows: Haloperidol (2.80 ± 1.6 nM) < Ethacrynic acid (4.70 ± 0.8 nM) < Risperidone (4.90 ± 0.39 nM) < Fluoxetine hydrochloride (5.40 ± 1.0 nM) < Aripiprazole (6.10 ± 0.7 nM) < Sodium valproate (386.0 ± 0.0 nM). Haloperidol showed the strongest GST inhibition among the tested drugs, even exceeding ethacrynic acid in binding affinity. This suggests its potential as a GST modulator in cancer therapy. Molecular docking studies revealed that the highest binding affinities were observed for Risperidone and Aripiprazole, showing scores of -7.350 to -7.576 Kcal/mol for 9GSS and -8.786 to -8.982 Kcal/mol for 5JCU. These strong interactions indicate a high potential of both compounds to effectively bind within the GST active site. The molecular dynamics simulation confirmed the stability and consistency of these complexes throughout the simulation period. Given the anticancer role of GST inhibitors, psychotropic drugs with significant GST inhibition especially haloperidol may positively contribute to cancer treatment.

title: Metabolite profiling and in vitro biological activities of an endophytic Cladosporium sp. AUMC 15471 isolated from Origanum syriacum L.
journal: Frontiers in pharmacology
abstract: Endophytic fungi associated with the za'atar plant (O. syriacum L.) remain largely underexplored despite their potential as sources of bioactive natural products. This study aimed to characterize the endophytic fungus Cladosporium sp. AUMC 15471 recovered from Origanum syriacum leaves and to investigate its chemical profile and biological activities. Identification of Cladosporium sp. was achieved by morphological and molecular approaches. Comprehensive metabolite profiling of the ethyl acetate (EtOAc) crude extract was conducted using complementary chromatographic and mass spectrometric techniques, including gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS), high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), and liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). GC-MS analysis tentatively annotated 32 volatile and semi-volatile compounds based on mass spectral database matching and retention index comparison, predominantly monoterpenes, sesquiterpenes, and fatty alcohols. Targeted LC-MS/MS analysis detected 11 metabolites that were assigned based on retention time and mass-spectrometric characteristics in comparison with authentic reference standards. Several of these metabolites have not previously been reported in an endophytic Cladosporium sp. associated with O. syriacum. The EtOAc crude extract exhibited moderate antioxidant activity in the DPPH assay (IC50 = 230.21 ± 5.96 μg/mL). It also showed low cytotoxic activity against HepG2 hepatocellular carcinoma cells (IC50 = 93.43 μg/mL), with cell death involving both apoptotic and necrotic pathways. In addition, the extract displayed antibacterial activity against six bacterial species comprising five foodborne bacterial pathogens and one an opportunistic equine pathogen, with inhibition rates of 67.37% ± 2.45% against Staphylococcus aureus and 59.39% ± 1.24% against Campylobacter jejuni. Collectively, these findings indicate that Cladosporium sp. associated with O. syriacum is a promising source of chemically diverse metabolites with potential biological activities.

title: In Vivo Metabolic Profiling of Suzetrigine in Thoroughbred Horses Following Oral Administration: Implications for Equine Anti-Doping Control.
journal: Drug testing and analysis
abstract: Suzetrigine (VX-548), a selective NaV1.8 sodium channel blocker recently approved for pain management, was investigated for its metabolic fate in Thoroughbred horses using liquid chromatography coupled to high-resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS). Equine urine and plasma samples were collected following administration and processed prior to analysis. Combining the present in vivo data with earlier reported in vitro liver incubations, a total of 12 metabolites (M1-M12) were identified and characterised, comprising nine Phase I and three Phase II biotransformation products. Five Phase I metabolites (M1-M4 and M9) were detected in vivo, formed through O-demethylation, C-demethylation, monohydroxylation, and hydrolysis of the amide function. Four further Phase I metabolites (M5-M8), previously reported by our team, were observed solely in in vitro liver incubations and were not detected in any in vivo sample. Phase II metabolism yielded three conjugated metabolites, comprising two glycosidation products (M10 and M11) detected in both urine and plasma, and one sulfonate conjugate (M12) confined to urine. Intact suzetrigine was the most abundant plasma analyte at every sampling point, followed by the O-demethylated metabolite M1, whereas in urine, the amide hydrolysis product M9 was overwhelmingly dominant and the parent drug accounted for less than 1% of its response. Intact suzetrigine remained detectable in plasma throughout a 192-h period, while M1 and M9 persisted in urine to the final sampling points. These findings define the metabolic disposition of suzetrigine in the horse and identify M9 and M1 as the most suitable analytical targets for the detection of suzetrigine misuse in equine doping control.

title: Prevalence and genetic characterization of Cryptosporidium spp. and Enterocytozoon bieneusi in horses in central and western Inner Mongolia, China.
journal: Frontiers in veterinary science
abstract: Cryptosporidium spp. and Enterocytozoon bieneusi are important enteric pathogens infecting humans and a wide range of animal hosts, including horses, and some species and genotypes have zoonotic significance. However, information on their prevalence and genetic characteristics in horses in Inner Mongolia remains limited. This study investigated the prevalence, species/genotype composition, and genetic diversity of Cryptosporidium spp. and E. bieneusi in horses from central and western Inner Mongolia. From May to September 2025, 325 horse fecal samples were collected from Otog Banner, Zhenglan Banner, and Abaga Banner, Inner Mongolia, China. Cryptosporidium spp. and E. bieneusi were detected by nested PCR targeting the SSU rRNA gene and ITS region, respectively. C. hominis-positive samples were further subtyped by gp60 amplification. Phylogenetic and haplotype analyses were performed to assess genetic relationships and diversity, and prevalence was compared among geographic, age, and health-status groups. The overall prevalence of Cryptosporidium spp. and E. bieneusi was 2.8% (9/325) and 1.5% (5/325), respectively. Two Cryptosporidium species were identified: C. hominis (55.6%, 5/9) and C. parvum (44.4%, 4/9). All C. hominis isolates belonged to the Ik subtype family, including IkA18G1 and IkA19G1. Cryptosporidium prevalence was significantly higher in foals than in adult horses (11.5% vs. 1.1%, p < 0.05) and in diarrheic than non-diarrheic horses (16.1% vs. 1.4%, p < 0.05). All E. bieneusi-sequences were identified as genotype horse1 and clustered within Group 1. Phylogenetic and haplotype analyses showed that the Cryptosporidium sequences were closely related to previously reported equid-derived sequences from China. C. hominis exhibited genetic diversity, whereas the E. bieneusi horse1 genotype showed a relatively conserved genetic structure. This study provides new molecular epidemiological and genetic insights into Cryptosporidium spp. and E. bieneusi in horses in central and western Inner Mongolia, including, the first regional report of the C. hominis gp60 subtype IkA19G1. The higher Cryptosporidium prevalence in foals and diarrheic horses highlights these groups as priorities for surveillance. These findings provide baseline information for future molecular surveillance and assessment of potential public health risks associated with these enteric pathogens in horses in this important horse-breeding region of China.

title: Pre-ride transport as a key modulating factor of plasma metabolites and performance-related physiological abilities in Arabian endurance horses.
journal: Equine veterinary journal
abstract: Endurance competitions impose high metabolic and physiological demands on horses, requiring precise regulation of energy metabolism, hydration, and stress responses. Transport before competition is a recognised stressor capable of altering biochemical and hormonal balance, potentially influencing readiness for prolonged exercise. Understanding how arrival timing affects metabolic status may improve both performance and welfare in endurance horses. To determine whether the timing of pre-ride transport modulates baseline plasma metabolite profiles and post-exercise metabolic responses in Arabian endurance horses competing over 80 km. Observational field study. Ten Arabian horses were divided into two groups to compare horses arriving 1 day before competition (Tr1; n = 5) with those transported on the day of the ride (Tr2; n = 5). Blood samples collected before and after the ride were used for untargeted liquid chromatography-high resolution mass spectrometry metabolomic analyses. Baseline metabolomics revealed increased oxidative-stress-related metabolites in Tr2 and higher carnitine-associated metabolites in Tr1. Following the ride, Tr1 exhibited stronger increases in lipid-oxidation and amino-acid-catabolism metabolites, whereas Tr2 showed attenuated fold changes, consistent with reduced metabolic flexibility and incomplete recovery from transport stress. Limited sample size. Arrival timing significantly modulates metabolic baseline and substrate-utilisation responses in endurance Arabian horses. Allowing at least 1 day of recovery after transport may enhance physiological stability, metabolic adaptability, and overall performance readiness.

title: Bacterial Isolates and Antimicrobial Susceptibility Profiles in Mares with Endometritis in Zhangye, China.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Equine endometritis impairs fertility, but regional data remain scarce in Zhangye, Gansu Province, China, a major production base for equine serum-derived biological products. This cross-sectional study investigated endometritis and associated bacterial isolates in 985 mares from five intensive horse farms. Mares with reproductive abnormalities underwent clinical, ultrasonographic, and cytological evaluation. Laboratory investigations included culture of low-volume uterine flush samples, biochemical testing, 16S rRNA gene sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Among the 156 mares selected for further evaluation, 35 were diagnosed with endometritis. This corresponded to an apparent prevalence of 3.6% in the full surveyed population (35/985; 95% confidence interval, 2.5-4.9%) and a detection rate of 22.4% in the selected subgroup (35/156; 95% confidence interval, 16.2-29.8%). Clinical manifestations were generally subtle. Thirty culture-positive samples yielded 38 isolates across six genera. Escherichia coli, Streptococcus equi subsp. zooepidemicus, and Staphylococcus aureus predominated. A single bacterial taxon was recovered from 22 (73.3%) culture-positive mares, whereas multiple bacterial taxa were recovered from eight (26.7%). Escherichia and Streptococcus isolates showed relatively high resistance, whereas Staphylococcus and Bacillus isolates exhibited lower overall resistance. Limited geographical coverage, small isolate numbers, incomplete antimicrobial-use records, and unexamined resistance genes constrained interpretation. These findings support early screening of mares with reproductive disorders and antimicrobial selection guided by culture and susceptibility testing.

title: Pharmacokinetics of Sulfasalazine and the Temporal Profiles of Sulfapyridine and Its Metabolites Following Nasogastric Administration in Six Healthy Adult Horses.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Sulfasalazine is an azo-linked prodrug of sulfapyridine and 5-aminosalicylic acid that is activated by bacterial azoreductases in the distal gut. Its disposition has not been described in horses, in which extensive hindgut fermentation may influence prodrug activation. This study characterised the concentration-time profile of sulfasalazine and the appearance of sulfapyridine, 5-hydroxy-sulfapyridine and N4-acetyl-sulfapyridine after a single oral dose. Six healthy adult Warmblood horses received sulfasalazine (16 mg/kg) by nasogastric tube, and blood was sampled hourly for 14 h. Sulfasalazine and sulfapyridine were quantified by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry; both metabolites were assessed semi-quantitatively as peak-area ratios. Sulfasalazine was measurable from 1 h and reached a median maximum concentration of 386.61 ng/mL (Q1-Q3 330.44-504.35) at a median of 5.5 h, then declined steeply. Sulfapyridine remained near the limit of detection for six hours, rose abruptly between 7 and 8 h and peaked at a median of 2794.00 ng/mL (2381.87-3146.14) at 9.0 h, approximately seven-fold above the parent-drug maximum. Both metabolites rose in parallel with sulfapyridine. This timing matches published equine orocaecal transit times, indicating that sulfasalazine reaches the hindgut largely intact and is activated there by microbial azoreduction. Systemic sulfapyridine exposure was substantial and should be considered in any therapeutic use.

title: Analysis of Factors Affecting Pregnancy Rate After Artificial Insemination in Lusitano Broodmares.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Artificial insemination (AI) is widely used in the horse breeding industry, but its success is often limited by different factors. Our objective was to assess the importance of various factors affecting fertility after AI, using field data collected in 125 mares over a period of 20 years, corresponding to a total of 860 mare-year combinations. The criteria defined for measuring fertility were: (1) pregnancy rate per breeding season; (2) pregnancy diagnosed at the 14th day on the first cycle and (3) number of cycles needed for a mare to become pregnant. Statistical analyses were performed using the GLIMMIX procedure of SAS, with a binary logit model with repeated records. The overall pregnancy rate per breeding season (PRBS) was 0.813 and at 14 days on the first cycle (PR1C) it was 0.546. The PRBS was higher when insemination was practiced early in the breeding season (p < 0.001) and declined with increasing mare age (p < 0.001) as well as with stallion age (p = 0.013). Mares presenting uterine pre-AI oedema had higher fertility at PR1C (p = 0.037). The mean number of oestrous cycles for a confirmed pregnancy was 1.82 ± 1.01 and, among others, age impacted this result adversely. In conclusion, our results suggest that some identified key factors can be used by owners, farm managers and veterinarians to improve mare reproductive performance.

title: Whole-Genome Characterization of a G3P[59] Rotavirus A Strain from a Diarrheic Donkey Foal Reveals an Unusual Genomic Background.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Rotavirus A (RVA) is an important enteric pathogen of neonatal animals, whereas the genomic diversity of donkey-origin RVA remains incompletely defined. In 2025, an RVA strain was recovered from a diarrheic donkey foal in Shandong Province, China, and designated RVA/Donkey-wt/CHN/SD2503/2025/G3P[59] (SD2503). Viral RNA was subjected to Illumina NovaSeq paired-end sequencing, de novo assembly, genotype assignment, sequence comparison, and segment-specific maximum-likelihood phylogenetic analysis. Sequences corresponding to all 11 genome segments were recovered, yielding the constellation G3-P[59]-I3-R3-C3-M3-A9-N3-T3-E3-H6. The VP4 gene was highly divergent: the closest BLASTn match was the P[24] rhesus strain TUCH, with 79.58% nucleotide identity, below the 80% threshold used to assign VP4 sequences to the same P genotype. The VP4 sequence was subsequently confirmed by the Rotavirus Classification Working Group as P[59]. Other segments showed discordant relationships. VP7 clustered with rabbit strain rab1404 with strong bootstrap support, whereas several internal genes grouped within genotype backgrounds represented by simian, rabbit, pangolin, equine, and other mammalian RVAs. The topological incongruence across segments, together with the unusual genotype constellation, suggests possible historical reassortment involving cross-species-associated RVA lineages, although the specific reassortment events remain unresolved. SD2503 provides an 11-segment genomic framework for an independently identified donkey G3P[59] RVA and supports broader genomic surveillance of RVA in equids.

title: Polypropylene Mesh-Augmented Soft-Tissue Reconstruction for Presumed Traumatic Lateral Patellar Luxation in an Adult Pony: A Case Report.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Patellar luxation is uncommon in horses, and traumatic lateral luxation in adult equids has rarely been reported. A 3-year-old, 75 kg female Shetland pony presented with severe right hindlimb lameness and minimal weight bearing approximately 2 weeks after a suspected traumatic event. The right patella was fixed lateral to the femoral trochlea and could not be manually reduced during conscious examination. Radiographs confirmed lateral patellar luxation without apparent osseous deformity. Following general anesthesia and surgical exposure, the patella was manually reduced. Treatment comprised lateral retinacular and fascial release, medial capsular imbrication and extra-articular polypropylene mesh augmentation. No osseous corrective procedure was performed. Radiographs obtained 2 days postoperatively confirmed maintenance of reduction. Partial weight bearing was observed approximately 10 days after surgery. No surgical site complications were observed during hospitalization, and the pony was discharged on postoperative day 12. At telephone follow-up 37 days after surgery, the owner reported that the pony was walking more frequently. An owner-provided video recorded on postoperative day 130 showed no overt lameness during walking; trotting was not assessed, and no further clinical examination or radiography was performed. Mesh-augmented soft-tissue reconstruction was technically feasible in this adult pony, although objective follow-up remained limited.

title: Inter-Reader and Inter-Modality Agreement for Radiographic and Magnetic Resonance Imaging Subchondral Bone Assessment in the Equine Proximal Phalanx Is Location- and Pattern-Dependent.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Standing low-field magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is widely used for subchondral bone (SCB) assessment of the equine proximal phalanx, but radiography remains the most common first-line imaging modality, and no direct comparison between the two is available for SCB sclerosis and resorption. Fifty-four fetlocks from 52 horses referred for standing MRI were retrospectively assessed at the medial glenoid, sagittal groove and lateral glenoid, using an ordinal scale for sclerosis and a four-type nominal classification for resorption. Seven readers of varied clinical backgrounds performed independent radiographic readings; two board-certified radiologists then established a consensus reading, blinded to MRI. Agreement was quantified with Gwet's agreement coefficients (inter-reader), weighted and unweighted Cohen's κ (reader-MRI) and symmetric metrics (consensus-MRI). Inter-reader agreement for sclerosis was location-dependent (Gwet's agreement coefficient = 0.27-0.73, lowest medially) and substantial-to-almost-perfect for resorption (Gwet's agreement coefficient ≥ 0.72). The radiographic consensus aligned closely with MRI at the sagittal groove but underestimated marked sclerosis medially and over-called it laterally; fracture-type resorption was reliably detected at the sagittal groove but misclassified medially. Radiography can be relied upon for sagittal groove lesions, but complementary MRI is warranted medially when resorption or clinical suspicion of fracture is present, and to confirm radiographic positive calls laterally.

title: How Driveability Is Conceptualised in Harness Racing: Insights from Trainer and Driver Interviews.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Within harness racing, the concept of driveability has received little scientific attention despite its apparent relevance to training, racing, and horse welfare. This study explored, through semi-structured interviews, how eight Swedish harness-racing trainers and drivers conceptualise driveability and relate it to performance, rein tension, equipment use, and horse welfare. The data were analysed with reflexive thematic analysis. Three themes were developed: (1) calm training is key, (2) one cannot always influence driveability, and (3) equipment is a tool. Participants described a driveable horse as calm, attentive, and responsive to the driver's signals. The findings suggest that driveability is best understood as a relational and context-dependent concept, shaped by training and ongoing interaction between driver and horse, while also being influenced by individual horse characteristics, situational conditions, and equipment use. Participants described both potential alignment and tension between welfare and performance. These perceived relationships require further investigation through independent assessment of practices and welfare outcomes.

title: Assessment of Oral Mucosal Colour in Horses: Initial Application of the Uldahl Standard Across Physiological States.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Assessment of oral mucosal colour is widely used in equine clinical and welfare evaluations, but inconsistent terminology limits comparison between clinical observations and research studies. This study evaluates, as an initial proof-of-concept, the Uldahl Standard for systematically describing mucosal colour and saturation. Gingival and lingual mucosae were assessed in clinically normal horses, healthy horses sedated for routine dental procedures, and horses with severe systemic circulatory compromise. Photographic colour samples validated against in vivo observations were classified using Munsell notation, ISCC-NBS terminology and the Uldahl Standard. Three illustrative cases of tongue discolouration were additionally assessed. Descriptive analyses characterised colour and saturation across physiological states, while clinically normal and sedated horses were compared using exact chi-square tests and logistic regression. Overall, 42 unique colour-saturation combinations were identified. Chromatic diversity increased with physiological compromise. Primary colour differed significantly between clinically normal and sedated horses for both gingival (p = 0.05) and lingual (p = 0.004) mucosae, whereas secondary colour and saturation did not. Grey was significantly associated with physiological state in both gingival (p = 0.05) and lingual (p = 0.03) mucosae. It showed high specificity but low sensitivity, including 100% specificity for lingual grey. Purple occurred only in sedated and systemically compromised horses, while blue occurred only as a secondary colour in systemically compromised horses. The findings demonstrate the feasibility of applying the Uldahl Standard to equine oral mucosal assessment and suggest that primary colour, particularly grey, may provide greater discriminatory information than secondary colour or saturation. Further studies are required to establish the diagnostic relevance of broader colour-saturation patterns.

title: Estimated Breeding Values for Monetary Earnings and Cutting Points in Brazilian Quarter Horses.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: In the Brazilian Quarter Horse (QH), cutting points (CP) and monetary earnings (ME) are key success indicators, yet their genetic parameters remain unestablished. This study estimated heritability and breeding values for these traits to guide breeding decisions. Performance data from 1661 QHs competing in official Brazilian cutting events between 1981 and 2020 were analyzed for three traits: total lifetime cutting points (CPt), cutting points at four years of age (CP4), and lifetime monetary earnings (ME). Variance components and genetic parameters were estimated using single-trait Bayesian animal models. Heritability estimates were 0.110 ± 0.038 for CPt, 0.110 ± 0.048 for CP4, and 0.288 ± 0.091 for ME. Although overall genetic trends were positive, in the last decade CPt registered the highest annual genetic gain (0.116). The findings suggest that both CP and ME could be considered as potential selection criteria, and evaluating performance at four years of age (CP4) may favor early genetic progress. While ME shows greater potential for lifelong phenotypes due to its moderate heritability, both traits exhibited comparable selection accuracies; therefore, definitive recommendations require further studies on genetic correlations and expected responses.

title: Genetic Diversity and Population Structure of the Kustanay Horse Breed Based on 16 STR Markers.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: The Kustanay horse is a riding breed developed in Kazakhstan whose genetic diversity and differentiation remain insufficiently studied. We assessed genetic diversity and population structure using 16 autosomal STR loci from a 17-locus panel comprising 12 ISAG core markers. Of 765 genotyped horses, 703 remained after excluding duplicate records and close relatives; the X-linked LEX3 locus was excluded from population analyses. Five groups were studied: registered Kustanay (KST, n = 32), Kustanay from Qazaq Tulpary (KT, n = 36), Thoroughbred (TB, n = 31), Kustanay crossbred (CROSS, n = 9), and undocumented origin (UB, n = 595). Expected heterozygosity was high across groups (HE = 0.661-0.725). Overall FST was 0.0088, and AMOVA attributed 99.13% of molecular variance to variation within individuals. The Puechmaille estimators favored K = 2, whereas Evanno ΔK peaked at K = 4; neither solution revealed clear separation among groups. Nei's genetic distances and PCoA were consistent with weak differentiation and similarity between registered Kustanay and undocumented horses. Unequal group sizes limit interpretation, and these findings do not establish breed identity for individual undocumented horses. The results inform pedigree recording and conservation planning.

title: Ultrasound-Guided Two-Point Transversus Abdominis Plane in Adult Horses: An Experimental Study Assessing Wall Sensitivity.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Ultrasound-guided transversus abdominis plane blocks may provide somatic analgesia for equine abdominal procedures, but evidence in adult horses remains limited. This prospective, blinded, randomized, paired study evaluated the feasibility, sensory effects, and motor effects of a two-point transversus abdominis plane block in eight healthy, standing, unsedated mares. Each horse received lidocaine 2% (2 mg/kg in 0.1 mL/kg per injection site) on one side and saline on the contralateral side. Responses to standardized mechanical stimulation were assessed at 21 sensory evaluation points per side for 300 min. The block was completed successfully in all horses without visible discomfort or procedural complications. No desensitization occurred on saline-treated sides. Following lidocaine administration, sensory blockade began at a median of 10 min, peaked at 30 min, and lasted a median of 258 (233-260) minutes. Desensitization was significantly greater at the stifle and intermediate horizontal levels than at the coxal tuberosity level. Transient motor impairment occurred in seven of eight horses and was severe in two. The technique produced multi-metameric desensitization, predominantly in the ventrocaudal flank, but limited dorsal coverage and frequent motor impairment may restrict its clinical application. Further dose optimization and clinical safety and efficacy studies are warranted.

title: Evaluation of Digital Tomosynthesis for Detecting Articular Cartilage Lesions in Equine Distal Interphalangeal and Metacarpophalangeal Joints: Comparison with Computed Tomography Arthrography.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Conventional radiography has limited sensitivity for detecting equine cartilage lesions. This prospective ex vivo study compared digital tomosynthesis (DT), computed tomography (CT), digital tomosynthesis arthrography (DTA), and computed tomography arthrography (CTA) for detecting artificial and naturally occurring partial- and full-thickness cartilage lesions in distal interphalangeal and metacarpophalangeal joints. Sixteen distal forelimbs from nine horses were examined under simulated weight-bearing (SWB) and non-weight-bearing (NWB) conditions. Three blinded observers evaluated 24 regions per limb, using gross examination as the reference standard. Sensitivity, specificity, and agreement were calculated, and mixed-effects logistic regression was performed. Gross examination identified lesions in 141 of 384 regions. Mean sensitivities (95% confidence intervals), reported for SWB and NWB, respectively, were highest for CTA [60.8% (56.7-64.9); 57.0% (53.4-60.5)], followed by DTA [14.7% (10.6-18.7); 29.1% (24.5-33.9)], CT [13.0% (9.3-16.7); 15.4% (12.0-18.8)], and DT [0.5% (0.0-1.0); 1.7% (0.9-2.4)]. Mean specificities ranged from 96.8% (95.3-98.4) to 99.7% (99.3-100.0). For agreement with gross examination, CTA had the highest pooled Cohen's κ. Contrast medium administration was associated with higher odds of true-positive and lower odds of true-negative classification. Weight-bearing did not consistently improve lesion detection. Clinical performance requires evaluation in living horses.

title: Feasibility of Serum and Faecal Interleukin Assessment in Equine Surgical Colic: A Pilot Study.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Cytokines may provide information about inflammation in equine colic, but their clinical relevance remains uncertain. This pilot study assessed short-term changes in serum and faecal interleukin (IL)-1β, IL-6 and IL-8 in eight horses undergoing colic surgery and compared measurements with six healthy controls. Colic horses were sampled at admission (D0), 24 h (D1) and day 7 (D7); controls provided serum at D0 and faeces at all three time points. Cytokines were assayed using MILLIPLEX and MAGPIX. Admission faeces were unavailable from 3/8 colic horses (37.5%). Serum IL-1β and IL-6 were below detection limits in 29/29 analysed samples (100%) for each cytokine. Serum IL-8 varied markedly without significant temporal change. Thirty-nine faecal extracts were analysed without faecal assay validation. Faecal estimates were generally lower in colic horses, with nominal between-group differences for IL-6 at D1 (p = 0.045), IL-1β at D7 (p = 0.033) and IL-8 at D7 (p = 0.004). No consistent temporal pattern in faecal estimates or significant association between serum and faecal IL-8 was detected. These findings do not establish the usefulness of these cytokines for clinical monitoring and highlight sampling and analytical limitations that should be addressed in larger, clinically diverse cohorts.

title: De Novo Genome Assemblies of Kazakh Horses: Adai, Zhabe, Mugalzhar and Naiman.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Kazakh horses represent an important cultural heritage of the Kazakh people, shaped over thousands of years across the territory of present-day Kazakhstan. Long-term adaptation to extreme natural conditions has led to the development of a unique set of characteristics that ensure the high survivability, ecological plasticity and economic value of these horses. Long- and short-read sequencing was performed for three breeds (Adai, Zhabe, Mugalzhar), while Naiman was sequenced exclusively with nanopore long-read data. The resulting reads were assembled, and the genomes were subsequently annotated. The assembled genomes showed high contiguity with an average contig N50 value of 9.68 Mb (9,681,711 bp) for Adai, Zhabe and Mugalzhar, while the resulting contig N50 was 17.09 Mb (17,090,216 bp) for Naiman, and average assembly length was 2.42 Gb (2,442,471,376 bp). These are individual reference assemblies that establish foundations for future comparative genomics and pangenome development. Gene annotation yielded 19,584, 19,941, 18,695 and 20,572 protein-coding genes for Adai, Zhabe, Mugalzhar and Naiman, respectively. These assemblies complement existing assemblies for future genetic analysis, research into the geographic and breed origins of domestic horses, and breed conservation efforts, and will contribute to ongoing equine pangenome efforts.

title: Matrix Metalloproteinase-9 Concentration in Peritoneal Fluid of Horses with and Without Strongyle Infection.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Strongyle infections are common in horses and can cause clinically relevant disease, yet their associated inflammatory responses remain incompletely understood. Matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9), a key mediator of extracellular matrix degradation and inflammation, has been proposed as a biomarker in various equine diseases. This study investigated whether strongyle infection is associated with increased MMP-9 concentrations in equine peritoneal fluid (PF). A total of 83 horses presenting with colic, weight loss, or faecal water were included, and strongyle infection was determined semi-quantitatively by combined sedimentation-flotation. MMP-9 concentrations in non-anticoagulated and citrate-anticoagulated PF were measured using ELISA, and non-parametric statistical tests were applied. MMP-9 measurements in non-anticoagulated samples were strongly correlated with the values from citrate-anticoagulated samples. No significant differences in MMP-9 concentrations, total nucleated cell count (TNCC), total protein (TP) or lactate were observed between strongyle-positive and -negative horses, nor across faecal egg count categories. In contrast, MMP-9 concentrations showed significant positive correlations with inflammatory parameters, including TNCC and TP, irrespective of strongyle infection. These findings indicate that peritoneal MMP-9 reflects non-specific inflammatory processes rather than strongyle infection. The lack of association may also reflect limitations of faecal egg counts and sampling site, suggesting that PF is not optimal for detecting parasite-specific inflammation.

title: Biological Effects of Advanced Platelet-Rich Fibrin+ (A-PRF+)-Conditioned Medium on Primary Equine Corneal Stromal Cells: A Proof-of-Concept Study.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Corneal wound healing largely depends on the activation of stromal fibroblasts, which coordinate extracellular matrix remodeling and tissue regeneration. Although advanced platelet-rich fibrin (A-PRF+) has emerged as a promising biomaterial in regenerative medicine, its biological effects on equine corneal fibroblasts remain poorly understood. In this study, primary equine corneal fibroblasts were isolated from stromal explants and treated with an A-PRF+-conditioned medium. Cell metabolic activity, viability, intracellular reactive oxygen species, wound healing, cell cycle progression, growth factor secretion, and collagen type I expression were evaluated using colorimetric assays, fluorescence imaging, flow cytometry, and ELISA. A-PRF+ significantly enhanced fibroblast metabolic activity, increased intracellular ROS production, accelerated wound closure and cell cycle re-entry, and stimulated the secretion of PDGF-BB, TGF-β1, and VEGF-A. Furthermore, treatment increased the percentage of collagen type I-positive fibroblasts, supporting enhanced extracellular matrix production. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that A-PRF+ exerts beneficial effects on primary equine corneal fibroblasts by stimulating their metabolic, proliferative, migratory, and secretory activities. These results provide an experimental basis for the use of A-PRF+-based eye drops as a regenerative strategy to improve corneal healing in horses.

title: Human-Horse Neuromuscular Coordination Across Sequential Conditions During Physical Therapy Utilizing Equine Movement in Parkinson's Disease.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: This exploratory, single-session, repeated-measures study characterized human and equine trunk muscle activity and human-horse EMG covariation during physical therapy utilizing equine movement in individuals with Parkinson's disease (PD). Nine individuals with PD and three horses completed pre-session quiet sitting (QS Pre), figure-eight riding (F8), stop-and-go riding (SNG), and post-session quiet sitting (QS Post). Bilateral surface EMG was recorded from three human and four equine trunk muscles. All analyses were exploratory and examined four outcomes: normalized EMG amplitude, zero-lag human-horse correlation, lagged human-horse correlation, and human-horse EMG-EMG coherence. Human normalized EMG amplitude did not differ across QS Pre, F8, and SNG. Equine amplitude was greater during F8 than QS Pre (difference 9.43 percentage points, 95% CI [4.27, 14.59]). SNG also showed greater amplitude than QS Pre (5.30 percentage points, 95% CI [0.32, 10.27]), although this difference was not statistically significant in the participant-level sensitivity analysis. F8 exceeded SNG in the direct comparison (4.43 percentage points, 95% CI [1.44, 7.41]) but not in the adjusted three-condition comparison. Zero-lag correlations were generally close to zero; SNG exceeded F8 by only 0.0056 Fisher's z units (95% CI [0.0004, 0.0107]) in the direct comparison, but this difference was not statistically significant in the adjusted three-condition comparison. When temporal offsets of ±300 ms were permitted, lagged correlation strength was greater during F8 than QS Pre (difference 0.013, 95% CI [0.003, 0.024]) and during SNG than QS Pre (0.011, 95% CI [0.001, 0.021]), with no difference between riding conditions. Median wavelet coherence was greater during QS Pre than F8 (difference 0.016, 95% CI [0.013, 0.018]) or SNG (0.013, 95% CI [0.011, 0.015]), while SNG exceeded F8 overall (0.003, 95% CI [0.002, 0.004]). Simultaneous human and equine EMG was feasible during the sequential mounted conditions, but the observed signal properties differed across outcomes. Because the conditions were administered in a fixed sequence, their individual effects could not be distinguished from order-related influences. These exploratory findings require confirmation in larger studies with counterbalanced task orders, controlled gait characteristics, and relevant clinical outcomes.

title: Equine castration in Sweden: a retrospective study of postoperative complications across field and hospital practices.
journal: Acta veterinaria Scandinavica
abstract: This retrospective study describes and compares the surgical techniques and medical protocols used for castration of male horses in Swedish ambulatory practices (Field group) and in Swedish equine hospitals (Hospital group). Data on patient characteristics, perioperative medical protocols, surgical techniques and postoperative complications were collected as documented in patient records of both groups. Descriptive statistics, univariable and multivariable analyses were used to evaluate factors associated with postoperative complication. The overall complication rate was 35% in the Field group and 13% in the Hospital group. This difference remained significant after adjusting for age and breed in a multivariable analysis (OR 4.5; CI 3.18-6.36). In the Field group 511/521 horses (98%) were castrated standing using sedation and local analgesia, incisions were left un-sutured in all horses (100%). The surgical technique was described in 230/521 records (44%), the open technique was used in 194/230 horses (84%) and the half-closed technique was used in 36/230 horses (16%). Complication and surgical site infection were associated with higher odds in horses that did not receive perioperative antimicrobial prophylaxis (OR 1.5; CI 1.01-2.36 and OR 1.7; CI 1.08-2.82 respectively). In the Hospital group, 554 stallions were castrated under general anaesthesia, and the incisions were sutured in 473/554 horses (85%). The closed technique was used in 503/554 horses (91%) and the half-closed was used in 51/554 (9%). Perioperative antimicrobial prophylaxis was administered to all horses in the Hospital group. Postoperative antimicrobial prophylaxis did not decrease the odds of surgical site infection in any of the groups. In Sweden, standing, open castration with un-sutured incisions was preferred in ambulatory practice, whereas a closed, sutured technique dominated in the hospitals. Field castration was associated with a substantially higher odds of postoperative complications, compared with hospital-based castrations performed under general anaesthesia. These findings provide locally relevant evidence to guide clinical decision-making and antimicrobial stewardship and may contribute to the ethical discussion regarding the use of standing castration when alternatives are feasible.

title: "A Healthy Zebra Not a Sick Horse": A Cultural Case Study of an Autistic Individual in the USA.
journal: Culture, medicine and psychiatry
abstract: Social communication is a key domain at the intersection of culture, medicine, and psychiatry, particularly when communication is medicalized in diagnoses like "autism spectrum disorder" (ASD). Clinicians and scholars debate dominant medical model discourses of autism as well as grassroots neurodiversity perspectives. Increasing influence of neurodiversity perspectives has yielded increasing clinical and communication science studies considering diversity (not deficit) in communication. This cultural case study considers how one autistic young man in the USA orchestrates twenty-first-century discourses about autism, reflecting on his experiences with communication, social disconnect, and sensory sensitivities. His case illustrates how autistic-led concepts such as the "double-empathy problem," increased attention to sensory-social components of autism, and the changing role of the Internet have substantially reconfigured the voices that autistic adults orchestrate compared with those explicated by previous scholars. These reconfigurations align with changes in medical models of autism that blur and blend with neurodiversity models. His efforts to build supportive, autistic-led spaces provide models for authentic interaction and reveal new tools for forming biosocial autistic community. This cultural case study therefore reinforces the need to avoid one-size-fits-all approaches, and the importance of a person-centered approach to meet the needs of everyone within the community.

title: Unravelling the phylogenetic systematics of the horse-hoof limpets (Mollusca: Gastropoda: Hipponicidae).
journal: Molecular phylogenetics and evolution
abstract: Hipponicidae are a family of sedentary marine caenogastropod snails commonly known as "hoof limpets". They are characterized by cap-shaped shells, and most genera develop, in adulthood, a highly specialized foot along with a distinctive horseshoe-shaped internal muscle attachment, allowing them to attach permanently to hard substrates. Here we present the first comprehensive, molecular-based revision of Hipponicidae using both a Sanger (426 specimens, 4 loci) and a phylogenomic exon-capture based NGS approach (18 specimens, 528-864 loci), integrating results with morphological and ecological data. This is the first step in a substantial phylogenetic revision of hipponicid classification that has long been problematic due to extensive shell plasticity and morphological convergence with other limpet-like caenogastropods. We identified 61 putative species, approximately two thirds of which are new to science, including several complexes of cryptic species that in some cases involve type species of their respective genera. Molecular evidence supports a redefinition of at least half of the genera currently accepted. Hipponicids emerge as a lineage with extreme adaptations to a quasi-sessile adult lifestyle, with the bulk of species having a horseshoe-shaped foot muscle that has almost completely lost its locomotory function, and produced a calcareous plate cemented to the substrate. This family also spans a wide bathymetric range, yet with most lineages restricted to either shallow or deep waters. Ecological data further indicate there is variation among hipponicid genera, differing in the degree of flexibility in substrate- and host-selection, ranging from specialized to capable of colonising the surface of a wide range of living and non-living substrates, but in general having pronounced shell plasticity in response to attachment conditions.

title: Effect of pentoxifylline and of penicillamine, hypotaurine and epinephrine on motility of poor-motility frozen-thawed semen in stallions.
journal: Animal reproduction science
abstract: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) allows equine embryo production from low-quality semen. However, some frozen-thawed semen has such low motility that selection of motile sperm for injection is challenging. To explore methods to increase sperm motility to facilitate selection during ICSI, we evaluated the effects of pentoxifylline and of penicillamine, hypotaurine and epinephrine (PHE) on both standard frozen-thawed (1x) semen and a model of poor-motility semen (4x, frozen and thawed four times). In Exp. 1, 1x and 4x semen was treated with 0.5, 1, 2 or 4 mg/mL pentoxifylline; in Exp. 2, 1x and 4x semen was treated with 2 or 4 mg/mL pentoxifylline, or with low or high concentrations of PHE (18 µM penicillamine, 9 µM hypotaurine and 1.8 µM epinephrine, or twice this concentration). Semen from three stallions was used for each experiment. Total (TMOT) and progressive (PMOT) motility were assessed by computer-assisted sperm analysis, and data analyzed using the Friedman test with pairwise Wilcoxon tests. In Exp. 1, pentoxifylline had no significant effect on motility of 1x semen, but increased TMOT and PMOT of 4x semen in a dose-dependent manner (P < 0.05). In Exp. 2, pentoxifylline significantly increased PMOT at 0 and 30 min for 1x semen, and TMOT and PMOT up to two hours in 4x semen. In an exploratory trial, ICSI with pentoxifylline-treated sperm yielded a 37% blastocyst rate (4/11), vs. 30% (3/10) for control sperm. We conclude that PTX, but not PHE, may have application to increase motility during selection of sperm for ICSI.

title: Physiological and fertility responses to alternative puberty induction strategies and fixed-time artificial insemination protocols in Bos indicus replacement heifers.
journal: Theriogenology
abstract: Three experiments were conducted to characterize the endocrine and ovarian responses associated with alternative puberty induction strategies and determine their impact on fertility of Bos indicus replacement heifers. In experiment (Exp.) 1, prepubertal heifers (n = 32) were assigned to either no treatment (CTRL), an intravaginal progesterone (P4) device (IVD) for 11 d, or a 150-mg long-acting P4 injection (iP4). Blood samples were collected daily from Days 0 to 12 to determine circulating P4 concentrations. In Exp. 2, heifers without a corpus luteum (CL; n = 629) were assigned to CTRL, 12 days of IVD with estradiol cypionate (ECP) at IVD removal (IVD + ECP), or iP4 followed by ECP 12 days later (iP4+ECP). All heifers were exposed to the same fixed-time artificial insemination (FTAI) protocol. In Exp. 3, all heifers (n = 2136) received the same IVD + ECP puberty induction protocol described in Exp. 2, followed by a 9-day P4-based FTAI protocol consisting of estradiol benzoate on Day 0, ECP and equine chorionic gonadotropin at IVD removal on Day 9, and FTAI on Day 11. Heifers were randomly assigned to receive prostaglandin F2α either on Day 9 (CTRL) or on Days -12 and 7 (PG). In Exp. 1, IVD generated greater and more stable circulating P4 concentrations than iP4 throughout treatment (P < 0.01). In Exp. 2, IVD + ECP and iP4+ECP similarly increased the percentage of heifers with a CL at initiation of the FTAI protocol compared with CTRL (P < 0.01). However, pregnancy rates to FTAI were greater in IVD + ECP compared with both CTRL and iP4+ECP heifers (P ≤ 0.05). In Exp. 3, PG decreased the proportion of heifers with a CL on Day 9 and increased follicle diameter, estrus expression, and pregnancy rates compared with CTRL (P < 0.01). Improvements in estrus expression and pregnancy rates were greater in heifers with a CL present at completion of the puberty induction protocol. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that use of an IVD for puberty induction and strategic administration of PG improved the fertility of Bos indicus replacement heifers subjected to FTAI.

title: Treatment of Relapsed/Refractory Aplastic Anemia.
journal: Indian journal of hematology & blood transfusion : an official journal of Indian Society of Hematology and Blood Transfusion
abstract: Relapsed or refractory aplastic anemia (AA) remains a challenging clinical scenario despite significant advances in first-line therapy. AA is an immune-mediated bone marrow failure characterized by pancytopenia and hypocellular marrow. In adult patients, first-line immunosuppressive therapy (IST) with horse antithymocyte globulin (ATG) plus cyclosporine A (CsA) achieves hematologic response rates of 60-80%, but 10-30% of severe AA cases will relapse after initial improvement, and a similar fraction may be refractory to initial therapy. Management of relapsed/refractory AA (R/R AA) requires a comprehensive, patient-tailored approach incorporating both pharmacologic therapies and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). Advances in the past decade have expanded treatment options. Second-line IST (e.g. repeat ATG or alemtuzumab) can rescue ~ 30-60% of patients, while the thrombopoietin receptor agonist eltrombopag has shown response rates around 40-60% in refractory AA. Newer TPO-agonists such as avatrombopag and romiplostim have demonstrated similar efficacy with favorable safety. Allogeneic HSCT remains the only curative therapy, and outcomes have improved markedly even for older patients and alternative donors. Salvage HSCT yields long-term failure-free survival superior to medical therapy in appropriate candidates, with 4-year overall survival ~ 80% in recent series. Notably, haploidentical donor HSCT with post-transplant cyclophosphamide has emerged as a viable option for patients lacking matched donors, achieving 1-year survival ~ 81% with minimal graft-vs-host disease (GVHD). Pediatric considerations include a lower threshold for upfront transplantation and unique supportive care needs. This review examines the current evidence (2017-2025) for treating R/R AA, including mechanisms of action of therapies, patient selection, outcomes, and adverse effects. We highlight real-world data, clinical trial results, and global perspectives (with a focus on resource-limited settings like India) to guide optimal management of relapsed or refractory AA in both adults and children.

title: Anti Thymocyte Globulin- Development.
journal: Indian journal of hematology & blood transfusion : an official journal of Indian Society of Hematology and Blood Transfusion
abstract: Anti thymocyte globulin (ATG) is a polyclonal antibody primarily derived from rabbit, horse, or porcine sources, used to prevent or treat T-cell-mediated rejection, graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), and aplastic anaemia (AA). It has demonstrated efficacy in reducing both acute and chronic GVHD and improving graft survival in hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) and solid organ transplant settings without affecting overall survival. Mechanistically, ATG depletes T-cells, modulates myeloid cells via PDL1 induction, and induces immune regulation. Rabbit ATG (rATG) is commonly used in organ transplants and HSCT. Horse or equine ATG (eATG) has proven efficacy in haematological disorders, particularly AA. Indigenous eATG (Thymogam) is widely used as part of immunosuppressive therapy (IST) in AA. Porcine ATG (pATG) is emerging as a therapeutic alternative in AA. Therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) has potential to improve dosing precision and immune reconstitution. Future directions focus on optimizing dosing, personalization and expanding indications. Manufacturing of ATG is complex process and requires multilevel monitoring and quality control to ensure efficacy and safety of the products for human use. This article aims to summarise the developmental evolution, composition, mechanism of action, overview of clinical uses of ATG, dosing, administration, and monitoring strategies, including the role of TDM and a brief description of the manufacturing process and various quality aspects of ATGs for clinical use.

title: Thrombopoietin Receptor Agonists Therapy in Aplastic Anaemia.
journal: Indian journal of hematology & blood transfusion : an official journal of Indian Society of Hematology and Blood Transfusion
abstract: Immune-mediated aplastic anaemia (IAA) remains a life-threatening disorder characterized by immune-driven bone marrow failure and consequent cytopenias. Frontline therapy includes immunosuppressive therapy (IST) with horse antithymocyte globulin (h-ATG) or rabbit ATG (r-ATG) in combination with cyclosporine, or allogeneic stem cell transplantation in eligible patients. Despite these approaches, overall response rates (ORR) to IST remain at approximately 60-70%,(Complete Responses ~20-30%, Partial Responses~30-40%) with relapse and refractoriness posing major clinical challenges. Attempts to intensify IST using agents such as cyclophosphamide, mycophenolate mofetil, sirolimus, alemtuzumab, or prolonged cyclosporine(CSA) have shown limited additional benefit, suggesting that inadequate marrow reserve rather than persistent autoreactivity may underlie refractoriness. Over the past decade, thrombopoietin receptor agonists (TPO-RAs) have emerged as important therapeutic options for IAA, demonstrating single-agent activity as well as synergistic efficacy when combined with ATG and cyclosporine. Their mechanistic rationale extends beyond megakaryopoiesis. TPO receptors are expressed on hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), and TPO-RAs may enhance stem-cell viability, promote multilineage hematologic recovery, and increase marrow cellularity. Additionally, TPO-RAs may modulate immune tolerance by expanding regulatory B and T cells, attenuating macrophage activity, and impairing dendritic-cell maturation, thereby helping to rebalance immune dysregulation. Eltrombopag(EPAG) and romiplostim are the most extensively studied TPO-RAs in IAA. Eltrombopag, an oral small-molecule TPO-RA, has demonstrated efficacy in both frontline and refractory IAA, with good hematologic recovery and potential iron-chelating effects. Romiplostim, a peptibody, has been primarily used in patients with refractory disease. Their distinct pharmacokinetic and safety profiles, including concerns about hepatotoxicity with eltrombopag and potential risks of clonal evolution with long-term TPO-RA exposure, require careful clinical consideration. Prospective studies, including the NIH cohort and the RACE trial, have provided pivotal evidence that adding a TPO-RA to standard IST improves hematologic responses and supports enhanced multilineage recovery with acceptable safety. However, rates of relapse and clonal evolution remain comparable to historical cohorts. Ongoing studies aim to refine optimal sequencing, dosing strategies, and combination regimens. The evolving evidence supports the integration of TPO-RAs into IAA management to augment marrow recovery and achieve more durable correction of cytopenias.

title: Behavioral Processes Underlying Oxytocin-Induced Group Cohesion in Free-Ranging Horses.
journal: Physiology & behavior
abstract: Oxytocin, a neuropeptide hormone, has been suggested to contribute to group cohesion. However, previous studies have primarily focused on interactions at the individual or dyadic level, leaving limited direct evidence regarding how oxytocin influences behavior within established social groups. In this study, we examined the effects of intranasal oxytocin administration on social interactions in a feeding context (i.e. affiliative co-feeding or competition over spatially distributed food patches) in semi-free-ranging captive horse groups. Specifically, we asked two questions: first, which types of social interactions are altered by oxytocin; and second, whether these effects depend on individuals' social positions within the group, namely centrality and dominance. We used drone recording and machine-learning-based tracking to detect co-feeding in the same food patch and approaches toward occupied patches, while aggression was recorded through direct behavioral observation. The results showed that oxytocin affected the tolerance of approaches according to pre-existing affiliative relationships but did not consistently affect active approaches or aggression. Specifically, oxytocin redistributed social tolerance from strongly affiliated partners toward more weakly affiliated partners. By contrast, we found no consistent evidence that the effects of oxytocin depended on individuals' centrality or dominance. This study emphasizes the importance of examining oxytocin effects on social interactions in established groups, in addition to traditional dyadic paradigms. The combination of drone-based observation and machine-learning-based tracking provides a high-resolution framework for quantitative comparative analyses, which should advance our understanding of the behavioral processes through which oxytocin shapes social organization.

title: Discrepancy between cross-neutralizing reactivity and protection in horses suggests inactivated vaccine antisera underestimate cross-protection against equine influenza.
journal: Vaccine
abstract: For equine influenza vaccine strain selection, antisera collected from infected horses (post-infection antisera) have been used for antigenic analysis. However, inactivated whole-virus vaccines are widely administered to horses, and therefore, the use of antisera collected from horses immunized with inactivated viruses (inactivated vaccine antisera) has the potential to be more clinically relevant for evaluating vaccine efficacy. The objective of this study was to determine whether inactivated vaccine antisera can serve as a reliable surrogate for post-infection antisera and whether they are appropriate for equine influenza vaccine strain selection. In the virus neutralization assay, post-infection antisera against a Japanese vaccine strain (A/equine/Ibaraki/1/2007) cross-reacted with the heterologous challenge strain (A/equine/New York/1/2017), whereas inactivated vaccine antisera showed a more than 10-fold reduction in cross-reactivity. However, in the experimental challenge study with A/equine/New York/1/2017, horses immunized with inactivated A/equine/Ibaraki/1/2007 showed significantly reduced rectal temperature, virus shedding, and inflammation marker levels, despite low cross-neutralizing reactivity, when compared to the unimmunized control horses. These results indicate that a reduction in cross-neutralizing reactivity of inactivated vaccine antisera does not necessarily reflect a loss of vaccine efficacy in horses. In conclusion, this study suggests that relying only on inactivated vaccine antisera underestimates vaccine efficacy against equine influenza. Although preparing post-infection antisera presents practical difficulties, their use remains valuable for the selection of appropriate vaccine strains.

title: Recombinant equine lubricin is safe and well tolerated following multiple intra-articular injections in healthy fetlock joints.
journal: American journal of veterinary research
abstract: To assess the safety of recombinant equine lubricin (rEqLub) injections in healthy equine fetlocks using clinical, biochemical, and histological outcomes. 6 adult horses were enrolled (3geldings, 3mares) in a block randomized, controlled experimental study. All 24 fetlocks were assigned to receive an injection of either 2 mL rEqLub (1mg/mL) or PBS at 1 of 3 time points. Recombinant equine lubricin was injected into a randomized forelimb at 28 days and 1 day prior to study completion, and rEqLub and PBS were injected into contralateral hindlimbs at 7 days prior to study completion. Clinical and orthopedic examinations were performed at baseline and prior to and 1 day following each injection; synovial fluid was collected for biochemistry, flow cytometry, and proteomics; synovial membrane and osteochondral sections were collected from day-28 rEqLub-treated joints and scored using Osteoarthritis Research Society International criteria. 3 sequential IA injections of rEqLub in 3 different healthy fetlocks were well tolerated and did not result in adverse clinical or histologic outcomes. There were no differences in clinical or synovial fluid biochemical parameters between rEqLub- and PBS-injected joints. Synovial fluid WBC concentrations and total protein were increased 1 day after injection in rEqLub-treated joints. IA rEqLub did not cause any detectable clinical, biochemical, or histological adverse effects, supporting the favorable tolerability and safety profile of rEqLub. The small sample size and multijoint design are limitations. rEqLub injections were well tolerated, establishing a basis for future equine efficacy trials to evaluate the ability of recombinant lubricin to mitigate osteoarthritis in a clinically relevant equine model.

title: AI-driven, qualitative GC-MS/MS-based endogenous steroid profiling with automated classification for sex cohort determination.
journal: Frontiers in veterinary science
abstract: The proper identification of sex cohorts is essential for anti-doping within the regulatory framework for horse racing, as investigations could be compromised if the sex of a stallion, mare or gelding were misclassified. The single-threshold approach is not very useful for assessing hormonal profiles in horses because of nonlinear relationships among testosterone and other hormones and metabolites. In the present study, an automated Steroid Detection System (SDS) was developed using PDF-based data extraction and characteristic qualitative metabolic profiles and peak intensity patterns obtained by GC-MS and utilized in AI driven model. A total of 291 post-race urine samples from Males (n = 122), Females (n = 102), and Geldings (n = 67) collected at Seoul Racecourse, Korea, were analyzed by GC-MS/MS in multiple reaction monitoring MRM mode. IS-normalized ratios of 10 key biomarker compounds were used as input features. The Random Forest (300 decision trees, balanced class weighting) had a 5-fold stratified cross-validation accuracy of 90.7 ± 2.3% with per-class accuracies of 98.4% (Male), 87.3% (Female) and 82.1% (Gelding). On a stratified held-out test set (n = 45), it achieved 95.3% accuracy, F1-score of 0.95, and AUC of 0.98, outperforming Logistic Regression (81.4%, 0.80, 0.85), Decision Tree (84.7%, 0.84, 0.88), SVM (87.2%, 0.87, 0.92), and Gradient Boosting (93.1%, 0.93, 0.97). The feature importance analysis showed that 5α-androstane-3β,17α-diol (EN3), testosterone (EN1) and nandrolone (EN4) were the most important classifiers with 61.2% of the signal. Multivariate steroid profiling using IS normalization and Random Forest is a powerful, automated tool for gender determination in horses for regulatory anti-doping control.

title: Case Report: Incidental finding of a perforating wooden foreign body in the jejunum during surgical treatment of colic in a horse: use of intraoperative infrared thermography.
journal: Frontiers in veterinary science
abstract: Equine gastrointestinal tract perforation by a foreign body is a rare cause of colic. Assessment of intestinal viability during exploratory laparotomy is crucial and is usually performed using subjective parameters (color, motility, pulse). Infrared thermography (IRT) offers an objective, noninvasive method for assessing tissue surface temperature in real time, as it correlates with local blood perfusion. In this case, a 13-year-old Italian Saddle mare was admitted with a 24-h history of acute, progressive abdominal pain unresponsive to medical therapy. Clinical examination revealed severe discomfort, systemic compromise (HR: 53 bpm, CRT > 3 s), marked leukocytosis (16,600 cells/mm3), hyperproteinemia (8 g/dL), and severe hyperlactatemia (15 mmol/L). Transabdominal ultrasound confirmed small intestinal distention. Emergency exploratory laparotomy revealed a 10 cm solid, irregular mass in the jejunum, causing obstruction and localized perforation. Intraoperative infrared thermography (FLIR ThermaCam E8) was used at three time points (T0: exteriorization, T1: margin selection, T2: pre-repositioning) to monitor surface temperature distributions. At T0, a distinct thermal gradient (Delta T = 1.9 °C) was detected between the viable intestinal segments (mean T = 35.1 °C) and the affected ischemic area (mean T = 33.2 °C). Based on the clinical examination and findings, a segmental enterectomy with end-to-end anastomosis was performed. Post-resection mapping (T2) confirmed equal perfusion of both stumps with a difference between measurements of: Delta T = 0.1 °C. Dissection of the resected mass revealed a wooden stick. The mare recovered uneventfully and was discharged 10 days after surgery. This case demonstrates that foreign body-associated intestinal perforation should be considered among the differential diagnosis of horses presenting with severe small intestinal colic. Furthermore, intraoperative infrared thermography proved to be an adjunctive method for real-time quantification of surface temperatures in the examined stumps, providing an objective assessment of surface temperature patterns to complement visual inspection during tissue evaluation.

title: Mechanical nociceptive thresholds of the foot do not change following anaesthesia of the digital flexor tendon sheath in horses.
authors: de Da Cunha Marina Souza Luz
journal: Veterinary record open
abstract: The selectivity of diagnostic analgesia of the digital flexor tendon sheath (DFTS) in horses remains debated. This study aimed to determine whether intrasynovial administration of 2% lidocaine into the DFTS increases the mechanical nociceptive threshold (MNT) of the dorsal lamellar stratum, sole, coronary band and heel bulbs, with correct placement confirmed by contrast tenography. Six healthy horses with no clinical or radiographic distal limb abnormalities were used. Forelimbs were randomly assigned, with one limb receiving 2% lidocaine and the contralateral limb receiving lactated Ringer's solution via the palmar pastern approach to the DFTS; both solutions were mixed with radiographic contrast to confirm accurate placement. MNT was measured in 10-foot regions using a portable pressure dynamometer before and at predefined time points up to 4 hours after DFTS injection. Data were compared using Friedman and Wilcoxon tests (p < 0.05). No significant differences in MNT were observed over time or between groups. MNT values rarely exceeded 1-kg force, and medians in both groups showed only minor fluctuations, remaining close to 0.5-kg force across the evaluated foot regions. Under the conditions of this study, contrast-confirmed intrasynovial administration of 2% lidocaine into the DFTS did not produce detectable desensitisation of the evaluated foot regions in clinically normal horses.

title: Prolonged wireless measurement of intragastric pH and pharmacodynamics of extended-release injectable omeprazole in horses.
journal: Journal of veterinary internal medicine
abstract: Adaptation of wireless capsules for intragastric pH measurement in horses has a short, variable attachment duration. Prolonged measurement is important for pharmacodynamic studies. Extended-release injectable omeprazole (ERIO) induces acid suppression for ≤ 7 days. Five-day dosing intervals are now recommended for improved healing rates. To (1) optimize the methodology to achieve 5-7 days of capsule attachment; (2) determine whether capsules can detect a treatment effect of ERIO; and (3) describe the pharmacodynamics of ERIO. Twelve healthy adult horses. Capsules were attached transendoscopically to the glandular mucosa on day 0 using either 1 hemostasis clip (1HEM; n = 4), 4 hemostasis clips (4HEM; n = 5), or a helix tacking device (TACK; n = 9). Intragastric pH was continuously recorded and ERIO was administered on day 1. Data are reported as median (IQR). Capsules remained attached and obtained data for 51 h (42-65), 129 h (105-256), and 95 h (71-154) for 1HEM, 4HEM, and TACK, respectively. The percentage of time the pH was above 4 (%tpH > 4) was significantly higher (P 4 exceeded 66% for 5 days after ERIO in 4/6 horses (66.7%). These refined, minimally invasive attachment techniques enabled longer, more consistent intragastric pH measurement. A treatment effect associated with ERIO administration was detected and %tpH > 4 exceeded 66% throughout the 5-day dosing interval in most horses.

title: Metagenomics analysis reveals horse feces as a reservoir of putative ARG-like sequences.
journal: BMC microbiology
