abstract: Despite the widespread distribution of horses and their close interface with human environments, the equine antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) reservoir remains insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to comprehensively elucidate the equine resistome by analyzing 104 equine fecal metagenomes sampled across China, thereby establishing a critical baseline for antimicrobial stewardship in equine husbandry. Through a non-redundant gene catalog approach, we identified 3,264 unique ARG-related coding sequences (CDSs). To detect distant homologs, hidden Markov model (HMM) profiling was applied, revealing 2,420 putatively novel ARG-like sequences. Functional classification indicated that over 90% of these sequences mediate resistance through antibiotic inactivation or target protection, whereas efflux and impaired penetration accounted for less than 10%. Taxonomic profiling attributed these predicted sequences to 23 phyla and 146 genera, with Firmicutes, Bacteroidetes, and Proteobacteria identified as the detected taxa. Furthermore, we identified 731 plasmid-associated ARG-like candidates, of which 446 is novel variants, predominantly conferring resistance to macrolides, streptogramins, aminoglycosides, and β-lactams. Experimental validation confirmed that the novel gene abc-f(9) significantly reduced macrolide susceptibility in vitro, elevating the tilmicosin minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of Escherichia coli from 64 to 256 μg/mL. These findings provide the first systematic characterization of the equine ARG repertoire, significantly expanding the known global resistome. Our results offer a foundational resource for assessing the risks of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) transmission and implementing informed surveillance strategies in horse farming.

title: Venezuelan equine encephalitis, Mayaro and chikungunya viruses as causative agents of febrile syndrome in Colombian patients during 2013 and 2014.
journal: Infection, genetics and evolution : journal of molecular epidemiology and evolutionary genetics in infectious diseases
abstract: Colombia's tropical climate and low-altitude cities create an ideal environment where mosquito-borne diseases can thrive. During 2013-2014, dengue was the most diagnosed cause of febrile syndrome. However, other viruses like Venezuelan equine encephalitis (VEEV), Mayaro (MAYV), and chikungunya viruses (CHIKV) were also present, and their true prevalence was likely underestimated due to limited surveillance. We conducted a cross-sectional study involving 90 febrile malaria- and dengue-negative patients from the Urabá region. For each patient, we collected both acute and convalescent serum samples, which were analyzed to detect antibodies against VEEV, CHIKV, and MAYV. Additionally, we attempted virus isolation from the acute-phase serum samples. We found that antibodies against VEEV were present in 28.3% of samples, CHIKV antibodies were detected in 5%, and MAYV antibodies in 1.7%. Notably, one patient seroconverted against CHIKV even before the first outbreak was recognized in Colombia in 2014. Furthermore, we isolated and fully sequenced VEEV, and our analysis revealed a close phylogenetic relationship with subtype ID Panamanian strains. This study highlights the need to consider arboviruses beyond just dengue (DENV), when evaluating febrile illness in Colombia. The detection of VEEV and CHIKV, even before they were officially recognized as significant public health threats in this region, underscores the need for enhanced surveillance and diagnostic capabilities.

title: Commercially available objective gait evaluation systems show good to excellent reliability in horses across hard-surface types and multiple operators.
journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
abstract: To evaluate the intrasystem reliability of an AI-based smartphone application Sleip (AI-SPA), the inertial measurement unit (IMU) system Equinosis Q Lameness Locator (LL), and the IMU system Equisym (ES) across 2 different hard surfaces and to assess the interoperator reliability for the 2 IMU systems. 8 mixed-breed research horses, aged 4 to 12 years, with varying degrees of gait asymmetries were utilized. To assess intrasystem reliability, horses were in-hand, straight-line trotted on either epoxy-coated concrete or rubber-coated concrete. Three trials were performed for LL and ES, while 6 concurrent trials were performed for AI-SPA. Interoperator reliability was assessed with 4 operators on the rubber-coated concrete only. Intraclass correlation coefficients and SE of measurements were calculated for 4 outcome parameters common to all systems as well as a variety of system-specific outcome parameters for LL and ES. Nearly all intraclass correlation coefficients indicated moderate to excellent intrasystem reliability (> 0.50) across the 3 systems (AI-SPA, 0.40 to 0.85; LL, 0.73 to 0.94; ES, 0.44 to 0.99) and were comparable between surfaces. Interoperator reliability was moderate to excellent for both LL (0.72 to 0.92) and ES (0.73 to 0.96). Standard error of measurement values remained relatively stable across study conditions. Despite inherent horse variability and minor differences in testing conditions, objective gait evaluation systems consistently produced measurements indicating moderate to excellent reliability and low measurement error. These findings indicate that observed changes in system output are unlikely to be impacted by operator or hard-surface effects, supporting clinical reliability of these systems in routine practice when utilizing manufacturers' instructions.

title: Standardized reference sera: advancing harmonization of equine viral arteritis serologic testing across national reference laboratories in the European Union.
journal: Journal of veterinary diagnostic investigation : official publication of the American Association of Veterinary Laboratory Diagnosticians, Inc
abstract: Equine viral arteritis is a contagious disease affecting equids, caused by equine arteritis virus (EAV). Accurate serologic testing is essential for surveillance, breeding management, and international trade. The virus neutralization test (VNT), prescribed by the World Organisation for Animal Health, remains the gold standard, but variability in quantitative results between laboratories limits harmonization. We aimed to produce and validate standardized EAV-positive reference sera to improve VNT consistency across European Union national reference laboratories, and to assess their impact on interlaboratory proficiency testing (IL-PT). Three sera from a vaccinated pony and one from a naturally infected horse were produced and evaluated for reproducibility, homogeneity, and stability. These sera were first distributed during an IL-PT campaign in 2013 to allow participants to characterize them and define expected titers and acceptance ranges. Once established, the sera were reused in subsequent IL-PT campaigns (2016, 2020, 2024) as positive controls. All reference sera had strong reproducibility, homogeneity, and stability. Their use was associated with an improvement in interlaboratory performance, with results within expected ranges increasing from 51.1% in 2013 to 81.7% in 2024. These standardized sera offer a robust tool for harmonizing EAV VNTs, improving test reliability, and supporting surveillance and trade.

title: Rare allergen sources are clinically relevant sensitizers in Central Europe.
journal: Allergologie select
abstract: In recent times, diagnosing allergies apart from house dust mite (HDM), birch tree, and grass pollen has become increasingly difficult because allergen manufacturers have withdrawn many commercial skin prick test (SPT) solutions for rare allergen sources. A cohort of 5,857 patients (mean age 35.9 ± 20.3 years, 60.5% female) was tested with standardized SPT panels comprising 46 inhalant and food allergens at a large allergy outpatient clinic in Vienna. Cases with positive tests and allergen-specific history were judged as "relevant", those without as "latent". In the patient cohort, 48.8% presented with a history of allergic rhinoconjunctivitis (ARC), 16.7% with bronchial asthma (BA), 13.2% with atopic dermatitis (AD), and 28.9% with food allergy (FA). Of 113,893 SPTs, 7.0% were relevant, 5.3% were latent, and 87.7% remained negative. The 3 most frequent allergen sources - grass, birch, and HDM - showed the highest ratio of 22.2% relevant compared to 7.1% latent SPTs. The 6 other non-rare allergen sources - European ash tree, mugwort, ragweed, Alternaria alternata, cat, and dog - yielded 9.5% positive and 7.4% latent SPT results. The other 34 rare allergen sources resulted in 1.8% positive and 3.9% latent tests. Plantain, horse, hazelnut (food), soymilk, peanut, plane tree, and nettle ranked top among the rare allergens. Among rare allergens, relevant SPTs to horse/rabbit, Alternaria alternata, oat flour, and rye flour were associated with an increased risk for BA including work-related asthma. 15.4% (1,230/7,985) of all relevant SPTs were observed in "rare allergens". This demonstrates the necessity of including rare allergens in standard allergy workups.

title: Fungal DNA in pooled equine uterine samples: an exploratory ITS2 amplicon sequencing pilot study.
journal: Frontiers in veterinary science
abstract: Fungal DNA in the equine uterus remains poorly characterized, particularly in mares without overt clinical uterine disease. This exploratory pooled pilot study used ITS2 amplicon sequencing to describe fungal DNA profiles in pooled uterine samples and to perform descriptive comparisons by subsequent pregnancy outcome and sampling method. Conventional microbiological culture findings were summarized as clinical context. samples were collected during naturally occurring estrus and, in mares that were subsequently mated, before the first mating of the studied estrous cycle. Low-volume uterine lavage (LVL) samples from 12 naturally mated Trakehner mares were pooled by outcome into a pregnant-LVL pool (1FR; n = 5) and a non-pregnant-LVL pool (2NFR; n = 7). The paired sampling-method comparison comprised a paired LVL pool (3LVL) and a paired SWAB pool (4SWAB), each constructed from samples collected from the same five mares. After bioinformatic processing, 82,862-130,870 reads and 27-111 final unique amplicon sequence variants were retained per pooled library. ITS2-target quantitative PCR detected 1,107-1,728 target copies/μL of pooled DNA extract. Neither the extraction blank nor the library-preparation blank crossed the qPCR detection threshold within 40 cycles; however, both yielded sequencing reads, and sequence-resolved control analysis could not exclude low-level laboratory or sequencing-related contamination. A targeted sensitivity analysis excluding the sequence feature shared by the library-preparation blank and two biological libraries did not materially alter the descriptive taxonomic composition, diversity, or ordination patterns. Ascomycota predominated across the pooled libraries (50.7-72.5%), followed by Basidiomycota (8.1-24.1%). The pregnant-LVL library had the lowest pool-level Shannon diversity value and occupied an ordination position that differed from the other libraries primarily along the first principal coordinate. The paired LVL and swab libraries also differed descriptively in taxonomic composition and ordination position. No fungal growth was reported in the available routine culture reports. These observations demonstrate the presence of diverse fungal DNA signals but do not establish viable uterine colonization, fungal infection, an association with subsequent pregnancy outcome, or equivalence between sampling methods. Confirmation requires sequencing of individual mares, comprehensive field and laboratory controls, standardized mycological culture, and integration with cytological, histopathological, and reproductive data.

title: Subcutaneous abscessation: An atypical presentation of Rhodococcus equi infection in a group of foals.
journal: Equine veterinary journal
abstract: Integumentary manifestations of Rhodococcus equi infection in foals are infrequently reported in the literature. Subcutaneous abscessation as the primary clinical presentation in temporally clustered cases of foal rhodococcosis in an equine farm has not, to the authors' knowledge, been previously described. To describe an outbreak of R. equi infection where foals presented with subcutaneous abscessation as the primary clinical sign. Clinical case series. Three Thoroughbred foals aged 6-11 weeks developed subcutaneous abscesses over a 3-week period in July 2024, out of a cohort of 11 foals. Thoracic ultrasound examination was performed on all foals on the farm, and 6/11 (54%) had evidence of subclinical pneumonia. No foals other than the three cases with subcutaneous abscesses were clinically affected. Purulent aspirates from abscesses in two foals were subjected to microbiological diagnosis and yielded a pure culture of R. equi. Two of the three clinically affected foals received 4 weeks of systemic antimicrobial treatment, and all abscesses resolved. Whole-genome sequencing of one isolate demonstrated near identity to a previous UK isolate associated with pulmonary rhodococcosis, and did not reveal genetic features that could explain the atypical presentation. Financial constraints on the farm precluded microbiological confirmation of diagnosis in the third foal. Sequencing of a single isolate precluded assessment of strain relatedness within the outbreak. R. equi infection should be considered in foals presenting with subcutaneous abscesses, even in the absence of overt respiratory signs. Exposure-related factors likely contributed to this presentation, and the possibility of a transcutaneous route of entry should be considered.

title: PLEKHG5 promotes equine herpesvirus type 1 replication and is associated with changes in cellular autophagy.
journal: Veterinary microbiology
abstract: Equine herpesvirus type 1 (EHV-1) is an important equine pathogen that causes respiratory disease, abortion, and neurological disorders, posing a significant threat to the equine industry worldwide. Cellular autophagy plays important roles in viral infection; however, the involvement of PLEKHG5 in EHV-1 infection and its relationship with autophagy remain poorly understood. In this study, baby hamster kidney-21 (BHK-21) cells and Syrian golden hamsters were used to investigate the role of PLEKHG5 in EHV-1 infection. The results showed that PLEKHG5 expression positively correlated with EHV-1 replication. PLEKHG5 overexpression promoted viral genome replication, titers, and protein expression, whereas PLEKHG5 knockdown significantly inhibited viral replication. Changes in PLEKHG5 expression were accompanied by alterations in the autophagy-related markers LC3 and p62 and in autophagy-related structures. Confocal microscopy revealed spatial overlap of PLEKHG5 with p62, mRFP-LC3, and LAMP1, suggesting an association with autophagy- and lysosome-related compartments. In vivo experiments demonstrated that PLEKHG5 knockdown reduced viral loads in multiple tissues and alleviated inflammatory responses and tissue damage. Collectively, these findings suggest that PLEKHG5 promotes EHV-1 replication and is associated with changes in autophagy-related processes, providing new insights into host-virus interactions.

title: B-mode ultrasonographic evaluation of normal thyroid gland in Turkmen horses: morphometric assessment and echographic characteristics.
journal: Veterinary research forum : an international quarterly journal
abstract: The thyroid gland is an integral part of the complex anatomy of the equine neck. Trans-cutaneous ultrasonography provides a non-invasive method for assessing the thyroid glands parenchyma and dimensions in horses. This study evaluated 30 clinically healthy Turkmen horses whose health status was confirmed through comprehensive physical examination, complete blood count, serum biochemical analysis, and thyroid hormone analysis. The horses were divided into two age groups: Group 1 under 36 months (three males and eight females), and Group 2: Thirty-six months and older (eight males and eleven females). Ultrasonographic assessment of the thyroid region was performed using a high-frequency linear transducer. Each thyroid lobe was systematically evaluated for its dimensions, volume, morphology, contour, parenchymal echogenicity and echotexture. Statistical analysis revealed no significant age-related differences in thyroid parameters; however, sex-based differences were observed: females had significantly greater thyroid lobe length and volume on both the left and right sides compared to males. Qualitative B-mode ultrasonography showed consistent morphological features; in the longitudinal view, all thyroid lobes exhibited a flattened, oval shape. On transverse images, most lobes (83.93%, n = 47) appeared elliptical, while the remaining lobes (16.07%, n = 9) were spherical. Irrespective of shape, all thyroid lobes demonstrated regular contour margins. Regarding echogenicity, most lobes were hyperechoic, with a few being isoechoic, relative to the sternocephalic muscle. Furthermore, all thyroid lobes exhibited homogeneous to mildly heterogeneous echotexture. This study establishes diagnostic baselines for thyroid evaluation in the Turkmen horse breed aiding in the detection and management of thyroid pathologies.

title: Arthroscopic Bone Xenograft Augmentation for Glenoid Bone Deficiency and Recurrent Anterior Shoulder Instability Improves Functional Outcomes Despite Graft Nonunion.
journal: Arthroscopy, sports medicine, and rehabilitation
abstract: To analyze the healing of equine-derived xenograft bone blocks with the native glenoid using computed tomography (CT) and to evaluate clinical outcomes in patients undergoing arthroscopic bone block stabilization with xenograft, Bankart repair, and upper-third subscapularis tenodesis for recurrent anterior shoulder instability with glenoid bone loss. Patients with recurrent anterior shoulder instability and glenoid bone loss between 12.5% and 25% who underwent arthroscopic equine-derived xenograft bone block augmentation combined with Bankart repair and upper-third subscapularis tenodesis between 2019 and 2023 were identified. Minimum clinical and radiological follow-up was 24 months. Xenograft healing was evaluated on serial CT scans, and clinical outcomes were assessed using Western Ontario Shoulder Instability Index, Rowe, quick Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand, and visual analog scale scores. A total of 76 patients (72 men, 4 women) met the inclusion criteria and were analyzed, with a mean clinical follow-up of 50.7 months (range, 24-75 months). Radiological follow-up on CT averaged 46.1 months (range, 24-72 months). All patients underwent CT imaging according to the study protocol. Western Ontario Shoulder Instability Index improved from 1335.7 ± 136.8 to 134.6 ± 138.2 (P < .001), with 100% of patients exceeding the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) threshold; Rowe scores increased from 35.3 ± 12.2 to 90.8 ± 11.0 (P < .001), with 100% surpassing the MCID; mean quick Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand improved from 42.6 ± 21.2 to 4.0 ± 4.7 (P < .001), with 86.8% exceeding the MCID; and visual analog scale decreased from 1.3 ± 1.1 to 0.5 ± 1.1 (P < .001), with 72.4% of patients reaching the MCID. Recurrence occurred in 4 patients (5.3%) because of high-energy trauma, and 2 patients presented Samilson-Prieto grade III osteoarthritis. Despite no radiographic graft-glenoid fusion being observed in any patient (0/76), graft morphology and volume were maintained without signs of resorption throughout follow-up. Despite the lack of radiographic union, most patients treated with arthroscopic bone xenograft plus Bankart repair and upper-third subscapularis tenodesis showed functional improvements surpassing the MCID threshold at a minimum 2-year follow-up. Level IV, retrospective therapeutic case series.

title: Co-encapsulation of Macrotyloma uniflorum protein and Pleurotus ostreatus extract in alginate hydrogels: antioxidant potential and phase-specific bioaccessibility.
journal: Journal of the science of food and agriculture
abstract: The development of sustainable delivery systems for bioactive compounds is essential to improving their physicochemical stability, bioaccessibility and functional properties in food applications. This study aimed to develop sodium alginate-based hydrogel beads through ionic gelation for the co-encapsulation of protein (HP) extracted from germinated Macrotyloma uniflorum seeds and oyster mushroom extract (OME) from Pleurotus ostreatus, thereby creating a hydrogel-based co-encapsulation system. Alginate hydrogel beads containing horse gram protein-oyster mushroom extract (HP-OME) complexes were successfully fabricated across HP:OME weight ratios of 1:0.1 to 1:0.3 (w/w). The beads exhibited uniform mean diameters (2.03-2.23 mm), whereas precursor colloidal suspensions showed good dispersion stability (polydispersity index = 0.28-0.34) and increasingly negative ζ-potential values (-21.40 to -30.90 mV). Encapsulation efficiency increased from 61.7% to 91.5% with increasing OME concentration. Results revealed that HPO-2 (1:0.2 w/w) showed maximum mechanical strength (hardness: 11.23 N), whereas HPO-3 (1:0.3 w/w) exhibited the highest encapsulation efficiency (61.7% to 91.50%), swelling ratio (6.06g/g) and antioxidant activity based on DPPH (i.e. 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl), ABTS [i.e. 2,2'-azino-bis(3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid)] and FRAP (i.e. ferric reducing antioxidant power) assays. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction analyses indicated non-covalent protein-extract interactions and structural reorganization of the polymer matrix. Simulated static in vitro gastrointestinal digestion showed limited phenolic recovery under gastric conditions and enhanced phase-specific bioaccessibility during the intestinal phase. The co-encapsulated HP-OME hydrogel beads demonstrated high encapsulation efficiency, enhanced antioxidant functionality and favorable phase-specific gastrointestinal bioaccessibility, highlighting their potential as a hydrogel-based co-encapsulation system with customizable mechanical and antioxidant attributes for functional food applications. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

title: RPA-assisted three-channel Cas13a-Cas13b-Cas12a fluorescence architecture for three-channel viral nucleic acid detection.
journal: Analytica chimica acta
abstract: Multiplex nucleic-acid analysis requires orthogonal signal channels capable of resolving multiple targets without substantial cross-interference. Here, an RPA-assisted three-channel CRISPR fluorescence readout was developed by coupling the distinct collateral-cleavage activities of LwaCas13a, PsmCas13b, and LbaCas12a to FAM-, ROX-, and HEX-based reporters, respectively, for detection of Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus (VEEV), tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV), and an eastern/western equine encephalitis virus (EEEV/WEEV) group target. The corresponding singleplex assays showed no detectable cross-reactivity with the tested non-target viral templates and achieved operational analytical detection limits of 10 copies/μL for VEEV and TBEV and 100 copies/μL for the EEEV/WEEV group assay. Integration of the three Cas-crRNA-reporter modules into one downstream reaction enabled discrimination of single-, dual-, and three-target combinations, with an analytical detection limit of 100 copies/μL for each target in the equal-concentration three-target mixture. Reporter optimization provided balanced channel responses, while inter-day repeatability and interlaboratory reproducibility yielded coefficients of variation below 10%. In a preliminary matrix evaluation using contrived equine nasal-swab samples, plasmid-spiked samples and unspiked negative controls showed concordant classification between the CRISPR readout and RT-qPCR, indicating compatibility of the assay workflow with the tested sample matrix. The method provides a three-channel analytical architecture that consolidates three downstream CRISPR readouts into one reaction while retaining target-assigned fluorescence interpretation.

title: Characterization of EHV-1 viral genes at the respiratory tract using a tracheal explant culture model.
journal: Virus research
abstract: Equine herpesvirus 1 is the cause of respiratory disease, abortions, and equine herpesvirus myeloencephalopathy (EHM) in horse populations worldwide. Current vaccines do not prevent EHM. Several viral genes have been implicated in systemic dissemination and viral transfer to the CNS, but their roles during early respiratory events remain unclear. This study employed an equine tracheal explant culture model to characterize the role of selected EHV-1 genes in viral replication, infectivity, and innate immune activation during early respiratory infection. Tracheal explants were collected from respiratory healthy horses and inoculated with EHV-1 Ab4 WT or EHV-1 Ab4 recombinant viruses containing deletions or substitutions in genes involved in neuropathogenesis. Viral infection was evaluated using complementary approaches including immunohistochemistry, quantitative PCR, TCID₅₀ assays, and RT-qPCR analysis of innate immune genes. Deletion of ORF1 resulted in increased viral antigen detection, elevated viral DNA levels, enhanced production of infectious virus, and induction of innate immune markers (TLR3, IRF7, IRF9, CXCL9, CXCL10, CCL2, IL-6) supporting the role of ORF1 in modulating epithelial immune responses during early infection. Deletion of ORF2 increased antigen detection and showed limited regulation of chemokines (CXCL9, CCL5). Deletion of the gI-gE heterodimer reduced infectious virus production despite limited effects on viral genome presence, while increasing the expression of TLR3, IRF7, and CXCL9, highlighting its importance in cell-cell spread at the respiratory epithelium. Additionally, gB4, gD4, and the N752 variant exhibited WT-like replication with only subtle immune effects. Collectively, these findings provide insight into viral determinants that shape early epithelial infection and may influence downstream disease outcomes.

title: Molecular Detection of Horse and Goat Meat Using the mtDNA COI Gene in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
journal: Journal of food protection
abstract: Meat adulteration is a growing concern because it compromises food authenticity, consumer confidence, and ethical or religious preferences. This study aimed to detect goat and horse DNA in meat marketed as goat meat in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, using mitochondrial cytochrome oxidase I (COI)-based polymerase chain reaction (PCR). A cross-sectional study was conducted from August 2025 to March 2026. A total of 427 raw meat samples were collected from licensed butcheries using a multistage random sampling approach. Genomic DNA was extracted using phenol-chloroform and salting-out methods and analyzed by conventional PCR using species-specific primers targeting the mitochondrial COI gene. A structured questionnaire was administered to assess meat-handler awareness of meat adulteration. Of the 427 samples analyzed, 368 (86.2%) were positive for goat DNA, whereas 5 (1.2%) were positive for horse DNA, indicating the presence of undeclared horse-derived genetic material. No amplification was detected in 54 (12.6%) samples, which were classified as inconclusive. Because only five samples were positive for horse DNA, statistical assessment of factors associated with horse DNA detection was not considered sufficiently reliable, and questionnaire findings are therefore presented descriptively. Awareness of meat adulteration was moderate, although the ability to identify adulterated meat by visual inspection alone was limited. Because the assay was qualitative, horse DNA could be detected but not quantified. These findings demonstrate the utility of COI-based PCR for meat species identification and support strengthening surveillance, laboratory capacity, and food authenticity monitoring systems in Ethiopia.

title: Ovarian insufficiency across the lifespan: Diagnosis, Monitoring and HRT controversies.
journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists

title: Targeted Dual-Responsive Probiotic Microspheres for Sequential Protection, Adhesion, and On-Demand Release in Ulcerative Colitis Therapy.
journal: Biomacromolecules
abstract: Oral probiotics show promise for inflammatory bowel disease but are limited by poor gastrointestinal viability, targeting, and colonization. We developed a multi-targeting probiotic composite microsphere (PCM) via scalable solution blow-spinning, with >20-fold higher throughput than electrospinning. PCMs provide three key functions: (1) pH-triggered probiotic protection: PCMs contract in gastric acid, shielding probiotics and increasing survival 2162-fold over free probiotics; (2) charge-mediated adhesion: negatively charged microspheres adhere to positively charged mucin overexpressed at inflamed colonic lesions; and (3) enzyme-triggered release: overexpressed hyaluronidase degrades hyaluronic acid, releasing viable bacteria via the "Trojan horse" mechanism. This sequential mechanism ensures high local probiotic density at inflamed sites. In DSS-induced mouse colitis, PCMs outperformed 5-aminosalicylic acid in alleviating inflammation, repairing the mucosal barrier, and restoring microbial homeostasis. 16S rRNA sequencing showed selective enrichment of beneficial genera and suppression of inflammation-associated pathobionts. This scalable, multi-responsive platform offers next-generation oral therapy for IBD and microbiome-associated gastrointestinal diseases.
